transcript: Okay, question for the theatre fans: What's your favorite two show day you've ever had? As in, “wow, the those shows were so good or so iconic,” “I can't believe I saw them on the same day.” This was a tough one for me, but I think I have my answer. I'm gonna give some honorable mentions first, though: I have a couple where the context made it even more epic. Like when I waited 13 hours in line to see Into the Woods in Central Park with like a very starry cast, including Amy Adams, Donna Murphy, Jessie Mueller. Then I went straight from the ticket line to see the final performance of Dogfight off-broadway, then went straight from Dogfight back to central park to watch Into the Woods. And of course, I have to mention the one time that I saw Wicked twice in the same day, which, like, I’ve never done anything like that before or since. I did a whole video about why I did that. I'll link that in the caption. But I think the best two show day I ever had was not only because of the shows themselves, but because I learned a very important lesson from it. I waited like 6 or 7 hours in the rush line to see Natasha Pierre and the Great Comet of 1813 on Broadway, right before it closed. Then later that night I saw Pipeline by Dominique Morisseau at Lincoln Center, which remains just one of the most beautiful, devastating plays i've ever seen. And the lesson I learned is that throughout that entire day, I was running on pretty much zero sleep. And yet both shows were just so exhilarating to me and completely held my attention. And to this day, I think about that every time I walk out of a theatre, saying to myself, “was I bored because the show was boring?” “or was I bored because I was sleep deprived?” And this might not be true for everyone, but that day I learned about myself that no matter how tired I am, if a show is good enough, it can still hold my attention.
